paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this little passage. Somebody is asking the watchman a question in the dark, and the watchman doesn't tell them the night is over. He says, "Morning has come, but also the night." (Isaiah 21:12) That's an honest answer, and it's not the quick comfort the voice from Seir was hoping for.

Then he says, "If you would inquire, then inquire. Come back yet again." (Isaiah 21:12) The door stays open. Nobody gets told to stay away, and nobody gets told to give up. I think the watchman is saying that a hard night is no reason to stop asking, and I know a little about long nights, because I had YEARS of them.

So when your own night feels long, keep asking and keep coming back. Don't wait until you have the whole answer before you show up, because the asking is part of the staying ready. This is why my ovens stay warm, friend. I can't tell you when the morning arrives, but I can tell you to keep showing up.
